newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-FRIESEN LIFTS CANADA TO WIN OVER FINLAND.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-FRIESEN LIFTS CANADA TO WIN OVER FINLAND.

text.p: Jeff Friesen of the San Jose Sharks scored with just over three minutes remaining to lift Canada to a key 1-0 win over Finland at the ice hockey world championships on Tuesday.
Friesen, taking a perfect feed from Chris Gratton at the blueline, charged down the slot and held on to the puck until he was on top of Jarmo Myllys then muscled it past the Finnish netminder.
The goal silenced the sell out crowd of 13,298 as Canada moved into equal first place in the standings alongside Sweden and Russia with four points.

"Our goal was to have 13,250 Finnish fans standing quiet listening to 47 Canadians sing the national anthem at the end of the game," said Canadian coach Andy Murray. "But it's not over, we have four points and so do two other teams.
"Unfortunately only two will play for the gold medal so tomorrow we'll have to win a very tough game against the Czech Republic."
Friesen was the most dangerous player on the ice throughout the game.
The speedy winger had appeared to give Canada the lead in the second period only to have referee Peter Anderson wave off the goal when defenceman Brian McCabe crashed into Myllys in the Finnish net.
The game was a goaltenders' duel between Myllys and Hartford Whalers's Sean Burke, who made two dazzling saves in the dying seconds to perserve the win.
It was the third shutout of the tournament for Burke, who turned aside all 23 shots directed at him.
"The score is an indication of the quality of the goaltending we saw today," said Murray. "Both Myllys and Burke were outstanding."
Each team enjoyed a powerplay opportunity in the final period but neither converted.
Canada picked up its man-advantage when Mark Recchi was high sticked by his Montreal Canadien team mate Saku Koivu.
